title: An Evening with Tyler Merritt
location: Davis Veterans Memorial Theatre, 203 E. 14th Street, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Join Tyler for an amazing evening of connection that will encourage your heart and remind you that Hope really does change everything 
HOPE: This Changes Everything Tour
An Evening with Tyler Merritt
What if hope isn’t something you wait for… but something you choose? 
In a time when division feels louder than connection and fear often overshadows possibility, Hope: This Changes Everything offers something different—an evening that will make you laugh, reflect, and leave believing that even small acts of hope can change the world around us. 
Join bestselling author, actor, activist, and beloved storyteller Tyler Merritt for a one-of-a-kind live experience filled with unforgettable stories, humor, music, heartfelt conversation, and practical encouragement. With his signature authenticity, Tyler invites audiences to rediscover what connects us, challenges us, and ultimately gives us reason to hope. 
Whether you’re navigating a difficult season, looking for inspiration, or simply longing for a night that leaves your heart a little lighter, this event is for you. 
Your evening includes: 
An unforgettable evening with Tyler Merritt
A post-event book signing
Audience Q&A
Music woven throughout the experience
Personal stories that will make you laugh, cry, and think
No matter your background, beliefs, or where you find yourself on life’s journey, you’ll be welcomed into a space where compassion, curiosity, and hope take center stage. 
Bring your friends. Bring your family. Bring someone who could use a little hope. 
You’ll leave reminded that while one person may not be able to change everything, each of us has the power to change something—and sometimes, that’s exactly how everything begins to change. 
Hope starts here.

description:
Hope is on the move. Residents across Yolo County are coming together for the
annual NAMIWalks Yolo County, part of the nation’s largest and most vibrant mental health
awareness event series. 
This year’s theme, “Together We Are NAMIWalks,” reflects the strength, connection, and
compassion of our community. Every step taken and every dollar raised fuels NAMI’s free
programs, advocacy, and support services – making a lasting difference for the 1 in 5 who
experience mental health conditions each year. 
NAMIWalks is more than a walk: it’s a movement. Participants leave inspired, empowered, and
reminded that no one is ever alone. Together, we are stronger. Together, we create hope.
Together, we are NAMIWalks.

WHERE: Woodland Community College | 2300 Gibson Rd, Woodland, CA 95776

All in our lifetime” said Executive Director Lou Enge. “The impact of NAMIWalks is deeply felt, in
families, workplaces, schools, and neighborhoods. This event is a reminder of our values that
when we work together— we are unstoppable.”

title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection
location: Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis, 254 Old Davis Road, Davis, California, 95616
description: This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.

title: Healing Movement Practice
description:
Iama Embodied Community
What if you gave yourself permission to slow down, breathe, move, and listen to what your body is telling you?

**Healing Movement** is a trauma-informed, embodied spiritual practice that creates space to gently connect with ourselves through movement, breath, music, mindfulness, and reflection.

Together, we’ll explore movement as a way of noticing and moving through the emotions we carry in our bodies—whether that’s grief, anger, fear, shame, joy, or simply the everyday experiences that can be difficult to put into words.

**No dance experience is required.** This is not a dance class, workout, or performance. There is no right way to move. You’re invited to participate at whatever level feels comfortable for you, with an emphasis on choice, gentleness, and listening to your own body.

### What to expect

* Guided, accessible movement
* Breath and mindfulness practices
* Music and periods of reflection
* Opportunities to connect with your body and emotions
* A welcoming, non-performative environment
* Freedom to participate in ways that feel right for you

This is a **pilot gathering**, offered at no charge. Voluntary donations to support the iama community are welcome, but never required.

**📅 Saturday, September 26**
**🕐 1:00 PM**
Come as you are. Move as you’re able. There’s nothing to perform and nothing to prove.

title: Talk Theology to Me: Questions about Faith & Life
description:
Iama Embodied Community
What questions about faith, God, Scripture, or spirituality have you been carrying around?

**Talk Theology to Me** is an informal, discussion-based gathering for anyone who is curious about faith and the questions that shape our lives. No theological degree—or even a fully formed belief system—is required. Just bring your questions and your willingness to listen and explore.
Together, we’ll have a facilitated conversation drawing from **Scripture, theology, and lived experience**. We’ll make room for curiosity, uncertainty, different perspectives, and the kinds of questions that don’t always have easy answers.

### What to expect

* A welcoming, low-pressure conversation
* Space to ask honest questions about faith and spirituality
* Reflection on Scripture and our own lived experiences
* Respect for different perspectives and places in the faith journey
* An opportunity to connect with others in a meaningful way

This is a space for exploration rather than debate. You don’t need to have all the answers—in fact, questions are encouraged.
**📅 Tuesday, September 29**
**🕕 6:00–8:00 PM**

Come curious. Come as you are. Bring a question—or just come listen.

### About the Facilitator

**Rola** is an ordained Presbyterian minister, yoga teacher, and trauma-informed practitioner whose approach to spirituality is progressive, universalist, and inclusive. She believes faith should serve the growth and flourishing of human beings—not limit them—and is passionate about creating spaces where people can bring their questions, experiences, doubts, and hopes without fear of judgment.
P.S. This meeting is not about teaching any particular faith.

Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

title: Imagining America National Gathering
description:
Join over 500 participants from the IA network and the University of California, Davis and Yolo Bioregion community (a geographic and cultural area that includes the cities of Davis, Woodland, Winters, West Sacramento, and surrounding areas) to engage in deep learning, collaboration, and transformative creativity on the theme of Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times. We will activate spaces across the UC Davis campus, in the City of Davis, and at community-hosted site visits. 
Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times calls us to re-story and honor the places, knowledges, relationships, and ecologies that have been made broken through centuries of violence and abandonment, and the current intensifying fear and repression. We know that our communities are tired, and we know that being together revives our collective spirit, giving us the strength and inspiration we need in troubled times. In this moment of upheaval, the 2026 IA National Gathering draws participants to Davis, CA in the spirit of mending the roots of our connections, and to “awaken,” as Buddhist monk and activist Thích Nhất Hạnh teaches, “from the illusion of our separateness.”

title: U.N. "Reboot the Earth" Hackathon
location: Peter J. Shields Library at UC Davis, 167
description:
In partnership with the United Nations, the UC Davis Open Source Program Office (OSPO)  and DataLab will host a "Reboot the Earth" hackathon. Reboot the Earth is a global initiative that addresses local climate and environmental challenges through open source solutions. 

Representatives of local agencies championing each challenge track will serve as subject matter experts; students will also have access to mentors.

 

Who: 

The event is hosted by DataLab and the UC Davis Library, and is open to students of all backgrounds and experience levels, from any university or college. No prior hackathon experience is required—just curiosity and an eagerness to build something that matters. Participants are strongly encouraged to form interdisciplinary teams and include peers from a variety of majors. Each team may have a maximum of five people and has to include at least one UC Davis student.

 

Why:

Contribute to solving a problem in your community

Get experience working on a cross-functional team

Release an open-source productThe winners are invited to UN Open Source Week at United Nations Headquarters in New York! Travel expenses will be covered for the winning team. 

Schedule:

Kickoff Day (October 23)Wrap-up and Judging (October 24) Participation is required for at least part of both days.

 

Learn More:

At UC Santa Cruz's hackathon in November 2025, the winning team, FireForm, built an AI-powered voice-to-text tool that lets firefighters complete required documentation by speaking naturally instead of typing. They continued developing it after the event, and it has since been certified as a United Nations Digital Public Good. 

 

At UC San Diego (May 2026), the winning team created FireLink, an SMS-based platform that delivers wildfire updates to residents with no internet or smartphone required.

 

This Open Access Week event underlines the UC Davis Library’s commitment to open science.

title: Author Talk: Market Memories Cookbook with Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan (Davis)
location: Blanchard Room, Mary L Stephens Davis Branch Library
description:
The cookbook, which has 92 recipes, arranged by season, also tells the story of how the county’s iconic market evolved as the brainchild of four young Davis people, including co-author Ann M. Evans, with a few farmers selling fruits and vegetables from the back of their pick-ups, to one of the most recognized farmers market in the United States. 

The story is told through personal essays by the co-founders and others with seminal involvement, 32 anecdotal quotes from vendors, shoppers, and elected officials, and a timeline chronicling market highlights over 50 years, as well as an in- memoriam page, commemorating the market vendors who are deceased.

The book is illustrated by Ann and Georgeanne as well, with beautiful pen and ink and watercolor washes for fruit and vegetables and flowers in all the seasons.

description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July). 
  
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site. 
  
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council. 
  
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org

description:
DJUSD Board meetings offer insight on how the school district remains responsive to the community’s values, beliefs, and priorities. The Board meetings occur on every first and third Thursday, in the City of Davis Community Chambers. 23 Russell Boulevard.
